query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled aging process that induces the in‐situ formation of nanoscale, coherent γ′ precipitates in a high-entropy alloy having titanium and nickel as the primary constituents will significantly improve its elevated-temperature yield strength and creep resistance relative to the same alloy processed without such an aging step.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast, homogeneous high-entropy alloy in which titanium and nickel dominate the matrix (with other elements provided in 5–35 at% each) and which shows a single-phase or coarse-grained solid solution microstructure without appreciable nanoscale precipitates.
generation.intervention: Apply a two-step heat treatment: first a solution treatment to homogenize the microstructure, then an aging treatment at approximately 800°C for 1 hour to promote the nucleation and growth of coherent γ′-type (e.g. Ni3Ti-like) precipitates.
generation.conditions: The alloy composition adheres to the HEA definition (5–35 at% each element) with Ti and Ni as primary constituents, and the intervention is applied under conditions where the aging temperature is sufficiently below the precipitate coarsening or dissolution temperature (e.g., operating temperatures up to ~800°C).
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a homogeneous dispersion of fine (on the order of 10–20 nm), coherent γ′ precipitates within the Ti-Ni-rich matrix.
generation.mechanism: The coherent nanoprecipitates act as effective barriers to dislocation motion—especially at elevated temperatures—by pinning dislocations and introducing localized lattice strain fields, thereby increasing the yield strength and enhancing creep resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to an identical alloy without the aging treatment, the heat-treated alloy is predicted to show a significant increase (approximately 20–30%) in yield strength at elevated temperatures (e.g., 700–800°C) and improved creep resistance due to the precipitation strengthening mechanism.
generation.baseline: The same titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy processed without the tailored aging treatment (i.e. as-cast or homogenized only), which exhibits a coarse or precipitate-free microstructure with lower elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected only if the alloy composition remains within the HEA compositional limits and if the aging treatment is conducted at temperatures low enough to nucleate but not coarsen or dissolve the γ′ precipitates; deviations in processing temperature or time outside this window may lead to precipitate coarsening or a lack of precipitate formation.
generation.uncertainty: The proposal extends findings from studies on Ni-Co-Fe-Cr-Al-Ti HEAs (e.g., PMC11396108::web::002) where γ+γ′ microstructures improved strength, and precipitation hardening results in CoNiFe alloys (e.g., PMC10532893::web::019), to a Ti-Ni primary system that has not been directly explored. Uncertainties lie in the precise kinetics of γ′ precipitation and long-term thermal stability in a matrix where both Ti and Ni are major constituents.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy using identical casting/DED procedures to ensure a homogeneous starting microstructure. Divide the material into two groups: one undergoes the proposed solution plus aging treatment (solution at ~1000°C to homogenize, followed by aging at ~800°C for 1 hour), while the other remains as-cast (or only homogenized) as a control. Conduct microstructural characterization (TEM/SEM) and elevated-temperature mechanical tests.
measurements: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to detect and measure the size, distribution, and coherence of γ′ precipitates
Elevated-temperature (700–800°C) tensile or compressive yield strength tests
Creep tests at elevated temperatures to assess time-dependent deformation behavior
Statistical comparison of mechanical property improvements (targeting a minimum of ~20% increase in yield strength)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heat-treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (≈20–30% increase) in elevated-temperature yield strength and enhanced creep resistance relative to the control samples, or if TEM fails to reveal a uniform population of coherent nanoscale γ′ precipitates, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The addition of elements with similar metallic atomic radii but different crystallographic structures (Al and Ti) to the Co-Ni-Fe alloy caused higher solution strengthening by the element with a different crystallographic structure than the solvent. The solid solution strengthening coming from addition of 5 at. pct Al to the Co-Ni-Fe alloy is negligible, while the addition of 5 at. pct of Ti significantly increases the solid solution strengthening. The precipitation hardening effect related to the presence of (CoNi)3Ti phase caused by the addition of 5 at. pct Ti is comparable with the total effect of the 5 at. pct Al and 5 at. pct Ti addition, which caused the precipitation of γ′ ((NiCo)3AlTi). Precipitation hardening is much greater in the investigated alloys than the solid solution hardening. We showed a successful way for effectively strengthening the FCC-HEA system (NiCoFe) using a small Ti addition. The microstructure obtained in the M3 alloy consists of precipitates with an L12 structure and structurally coherent with FCC matrix. We showed one of the ways of searching for new high-entropy alloys.

The microstructure, RT, and high-temperature mechanical properties of the RHEAs in the as-cast state were systematically analyzed, and the deformation mechanism was also studied by taking the NbTiAl-3 RHEA as an example, with the following specific conclusions: The RHEAs exhibit an excellent combination of high yield strength, low density (7.41~7.51 g/cm3), and large plasticity (ε > 0.35) at RT. The SYSs of the NbTiAl-3 RHEA are ~131 MPa·cm3/g at 1023 K and ~104.2 MPa·cm3/g at 1123 K, respectively, which are far superior to most typical RHEAs. These excellent mechanical properties are mainly attributed to the solid solution strengthening induced by the Zr element. The deformation of the NbTiAl-3 RHEA at 298 K is dominated by the planar slip of dislocations, resulting in two dislocation slip bands oriented in the [111](101_) and [111](112_) directions. A series of lightweight Ti-rich MEAs with minor additions of Zr were successfully fabricated through various TMT processing routes. On the basis of the experiment results, the microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of the alloys are summarized as follows: The XRD results confirm that the structure of the Ti-rich MEAs maintained a single BCC phase not only when they were in an as-cast state but also after they underwent TMT processing. The addition of Zr tended to increase the grain size of cast ingots and compensate for the effect of solid solution strengthening due to Zr additions. Therefore, although the increase in yield strength achieved by increasing the Zr of the as-cast alloys was nonsignificant, the ductility of the alloys remained mostly unchanged. The grain size can be refined effectively after hot rolling, and refined grains contain more grain boundaries that accumulate more strain energy, which reduces the initial recrystallization temperature. Therefore, the sample that underwent HR50CR70 processing had a low initial recrystallization temperature.
